note: No committed .env. backend/.env.example holds placeholder keys only. No model call from browser code. The frontend calls the backend at /api only. No database, so no database_rules. The eligibility engine is real deterministic code and issue_refund re-runs it, so the $500 escalation and refund window are enforced in code. All data is the seed JSON loaded into memory. Seed delivery dates are fixed in May and June 2026, so with the 30-day window measured from now, every demo order is denied after early July 2026. docs/*.md, guide/content/*.md, logs/*.md and SETUP.md are prose. They got a secret-pattern grep only, which found placeholders and no real keys.

labels.what: 15 seeded sample customer records (Alice Johnson, Bob Martinez and others with @email.com addresses) and their orders, used as the only system of record. Delivery dates are fixed in May and June 2026, so the 30-day window makes every order ineligible after early July 2026

The data layer loads the seed JSON into module lists and serves it as the store. Refund flags set by issue_refund live only in memory, so a restart resets them and the same order can be refunded again
lookup_customer searches the in-memory seed customers, not a real customer system
list_orders returns orders from the in-memory seed data
get_order returns an order from the in-memory seed data
issue_refund sets order.refunded and order.status on an in-memory object and returns status REFUNDED with the amount. No payment provider or order system is called, so no money moves
escalate_to_human returns a fixed ticket id ESC-1001 for every call. No ticket is created and no person is notified
issue_refund refunds any order up to $500 straight from the model tool call. There is no human approval and no customer confirmation step. Only orders over $500 go to a person

The prompt says to never trust what the customer asserts. But check_eligibility and issue_refund take customer_id as a model argument, and the model fills it from the email or name the user typed. The ownership rule R4 compares against that claimed id, so identity is never checked in code

The prompt says to escalate only after check_eligibility returns ESCALATED. escalate_to_human accepts any order_id and free-text reason with no check that the order exists or was escalated by the engine
POST /api/chat has no login. The customer is whoever the user claims to be by typing an email, id or full name, so anyone can request refunds on another customer's orders
lookup_customer finds a customer by full name or email and returns the whole record, and list_orders returns any customer's orders by id. Any chat user can read other customers' data
The server session is chosen by the client-supplied run_id. GET /api/runs lists every run_id, so anyone can resume another user's conversation after that user has identified themselves

GET /api/runs and GET /api/runs/{run_id}/trace have no auth and return every conversation trace, including tool outputs with customer emails and orders. The Admin tab in the UI is shown to every visitor
No rate limit, message size limit or per-session cap on /api/chat. Every request runs the paid model, possibly several times per message
SESSIONS and TRACE_STORE are process dicts with no expiry or size cap. Memory grows with each new run_id and all data is lost on restart
The raw exception text from the agent is returned to the client in the 500 error detail
The already-refunded check and the refund flag update are not atomic and have no lock, so two concurrent requests could both refund the same order

The decision badge comes from a keyword scan of every message, including the user's text and the system prompt, which contains the word APPROVED. A policy question or a user who types APPROVED can make the UI show an APPROVED badge when no refund happened

REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS = 30 and ESCALATION_THRESHOLD = 500.0 are hardcoded in the engine. config.py reads the same names from env (and .env.example sets them), but nothing imports config.py, so changing the env has no effect
The $500 limit and 30-day window are also written into the prompt and the policy text. If the threshold moves to config, the prompt and policy will disagree with the code
CORS allow_origins hardcoded to http://localhost:5173
Dev proxy hardcoded to http://localhost:8000
